subject: EchoHealth: Keepalive failures, streaming timeouts and retry amplification
messages:
From: Sarah Li <sarah.li@echohealth.com>
To: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek@redwood.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>
Cc: Platform Team <platform@echohealth.com>
Date: Fri, 18 Sep 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Production: multiple streaming sessions timing out + 5xx spike

Hi Vivek / Neha,

We started seeing widespread failures in our interactive note-taking feature this morning around 08:30 PDT. Symptoms: clients intermittently drop the streaming connection with a client-side timeout at ~15s, the server logs show bursts of 429 and 5xx from the Redwood endpoint, and we see large retry cascades from our frontend. Impact: ~22% of active sessions experienced at least one abort; two enterprise customers reported user-facing failures.

I've attached a trimmed log (echohealth_debug_0918.log) and a short screenshot of the token-level latency spike. Can you confirm whether this is a Redwood-side degradation or anything we recently changed on EchoHealth that could trigger keepalive failures? We have an urgent exec call scheduled at 11:00 if we need to escalate.

Thanks,
Sarah
Sr. SRE, EchoHealth

Cc: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 18 Sep 2026 09:28:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Production: multiple streaming sessions timing out + 5xx spike

Hi Sarah — thanks for the heads up and logs. We’re seeing correlated error-rate increases and a 15–25% P95 token-latency uplift for the model pool serving EchoHealth traffic between 08:10–09:00 PDT. Initial hypothesis: a transient burst of slow tail latencies triggered client-side timeouts which in turn caused repeat open attempts, amplifying concurrent load and causing upstream 5xx/429s.

Immediate next steps I’ve kicked off:
- Marissa is running targeted diagnostics on the Dedicated pool handling your traffic (collecting kernel stalls, queue depth, and batching histograms).
- We’ll temporarily enable a conservative keepalive / connection-throttle policy for your route to limit parallel session reconnects.
- Request: please share your frontend retry/backoff settings and whether any client-side change was deployed this morning.

I’ll join the 11:00 call and loop in product leadership if we need SLA reconciliation. Short-term mitigation plan is in PLAYBOOK_KEEPALIVE.md (attached) — Marissa, can you add the per-route command we should run?

Vivek
Head of Customer Success, Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: Production: multiple streaming sessions timing out + 5xx spike

On Fri, Sep 18, 2026 at 09:28 AM Vivek Kulkarni <vivek@redwood.com> wrote:
> Initial hypothesis: a transient burst of slow tail latencies triggered client-side timeouts which in turn caused repeat open attempts, amplifying concurrent load and causing upstream 5xx/429s.

Confirmed — trace samples show a cluster of requests with KV-cache cold starts and tail kernel preemption at ~08:22. Two actions we executed at 09:05 that should reduce immediate impact:
1) Adjusted per-route max-concurrent-sessions from 850 -> 400 for EchoHealth route (throttle to break retry multiplier).
2) Enabled prefix-KV prewarm for hot client IPs to reduce cold-starts for new conversations.

Longer-term recommendations:
- Enforce exponential backoff + jitter client-side (min 250ms, cap 5s) to avoid synchronized reconnects.
- Maintain a 20s server-side keepalive and a 10s client read timeout; current EchoHealth client read timeout at 15s is too aggressive given observed P95 token latencies.
- Consider switching affected flows to short-poll fallback after 3 failed streaming open attempts.

I’ve uploaded the operational playbook to the ticket (PLAYBOOK_KEEPALIVE.md). Attaching a small metric snapshot (redwood_stream_metrics_0918.png).

Marissa
SRE, Redwood Inference

Thanks for the quick responses. A few notes from our side:
- We rolled a small client-side change at 07:50 that touched connection reuse in the browser SDK — reverting now but it was live for ~20 minutes before we saw errors.
- Our telemetry shows a retry burst pattern that aligns with your description.

Two asks:
1) Can Redwood provide an emergency config that forces a soft-fallback to poll after 2 failed stream opens? We need a mitigation while we harden the SDK.
2) We will likely ask for SLA credits if this is classified as a service degradation — want to understand the timeline and RCA.

We’ll be on the 11:00 call.

—James
Lead Product Engineer, EchoHealth

Folks — looping in product and engineering leadership for exec visibility. Summary: transient kernel preemptions + KV cold-starts coincided with a small EchoHealth SDK change that reduced client-side socket reuse. That combination produced synchronized reconnects, elevated 429/5xx, and client timeouts (15s read).

Immediate asks for the team:
- Engineering (Rachel): confirm whether we can push a per-route soft-fallback gate that returns 202 + poll token after N failed stream opens; estimated ETA?
- SRE (Marissa): keep the throttle in place and capture additional flamegraphs; prepare an RCA timeline (24/72 hour cadence).
- Sales (Aditya): coordinate customer comms and start documenting potential credit exposure and renewal risk for DEAL-3497.

Sarah / James — we’ll prioritize an RCA and propose remediation and credit assessment on Monday. Appreciate your partnership and we’ll use the 11:00 call to align on immediate user-impact mitigations.

Vivek
Head of Customer Success, Redwood Inference
